verdict.rationale: 1Password's own docs show it saves passkeys and uses them to sign in through its browser extension, which keeps passkeys in 1Password rather than a single platform vendor's keychain. The pack never explicitly documents passkey sync across iOS, Android, Windows and Linux devices. Linux client complaints in the community are older and general, and a later user praises its Linux support, so there is no concrete contradiction. missing for 10: explicit documentation of passkey sync across iOS, Android, Windows and Linux; passkey use in native mobile apps; independent hands-on corroboration of cross-ecosystem passkey use.

support.subject: As a power user, my passkeys sync across ecosystems — iOS, Android, Windows, Linux, browsers — instead of being locked to one platform vendor

citations.quote: you can now create, manage, and sign in with passkeys on a growing number of websites and apps directly from the 1Password browser extension
You can use 1Password to save the passkeys you create for your accounts and sign in to websites with passkeys in your browser.
